the curvature bound. The initial coefficient can be conditioned
on its initial history throughout these arguments.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:threshold-smooth}
If the population is $L$-smooth, put
$\ell_{\rm s}=\log_2(1+\mathcal H_{\rm s}/h_{\rm ref})$. Then
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{\mathbb E[h_{\rm init}R_u^2]}{2A_N}
 +\frac{[(28+2\ell_{\rm s})L+h_{\rm ref}]D^2}{N^2}
 \nonumber\\
 &+\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0D}{\sqrt T}
 +\frac{4\sqrt2(1+\ell_{\rm s})d^{1/4}M_2D}
             {\sqrt N\sqrt T}.
 \label{eq:threshold-smooth-risk}
\end{align}
With $h_{\rm init}=h_{\rm ref}=h_0$ and
$\sigma_0^2\le CdM_2^2$, the order is
$\widetilde O((L+h_0)D^2/N^2+\sqrt dM_2D/\sqrt T)$.
Only the displayed logarithm is suppressed.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Use the smooth form of \eqref{eq:threshold-risk}.
The identities $A_N\ge N^2/2$ and $A_N/N^2\le1$ give
\[
 \frac{2D^2}{A_N}+\frac{3D^2}{N^2}\le7D^2/N^2,\qquad
 LD^2\ell_{\rm s}/A_N\le2LD^2\ell_{\rm s}/N^2.
\]
The vector-noise contribution is, more precisely,
\[
 \left(\frac{2D^2}{A_N}+\frac{3D^2}{N^2}\right)
 \frac{c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0A_N}{D\sqrt T}
 =\frac{c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0D}{\sqrt T}
       (2+3A_N/N^2)
 \le\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0D}{\sqrt T}.
\]
Bound the remaining radial term by
\eqref{eq:threshold-public-moments}. This proves the displayed
inequality. For the dimensional specialization use $R_u\le D$,
$d^{1/4}/\sqrt N\le\sqrt d$ and
$\sigma_0\le\sqrt{Cd}M_2$. None of $L,M,M_2$ is an input.
The comparator can be the original population optimizer.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{cor:threshold-nonsmooth}
Put $\ell_{\rm ns}=\log_2(1+\mathcal H_{\rm ns}/h_{\rm ref})$.
Then
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{\mathbb E[h_{\rm init}R_u^2]}{2A_N}
 +\frac{h_{\rm ref}D^2}{N^2}
 +[(42+14\sqrt2)d^{1/4}+4\ell_{\rm ns}]\frac{MD}{N}\nonumber\\
 &+\frac{28\sqrt dMD^2}{\gamma_{\max} N^2}
 +\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0D}{\sqrt T}
 +\frac{56d^{1/4}M_2D}{\sqrt T}\nonumber\\
 &+\frac{4\sqrt2(1+\ell_{\rm ns})d^{1/4}M_2D}
             {\sqrt N\sqrt T}.
 \label{eq:threshold-nonsmooth-risk}
\end{align}
If $h_{\rm init}=h_{\rm ref}=h_0$,
$\gamma_{\max}\ge d^{1/4}D/N$ and $\sigma_0^2\le CdM_2^2$, the
same controller has order
$\widetilde O(h_0D^2/N^2+d^{1/4}MD/N+\sqrt dM_2D/\sqrt T)$.
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Use
\[
 \Gamma^{-1}\le\gamma_{\max}^{-1}+N/(d^{1/4}D),\qquad
 (4+2\sqrt2)d^{1/4}+2\le(6+2\sqrt2)d^{1/4},\qquad
 \omega_{\rm rad}\le4\sqrt2M_2N/\sqrt T
\]
in \eqref{eq:adaptive-main-Hns}.
Multiplication by at most $7D^2/N^2$ gives the respective
coefficients $28$, $42+14\sqrt2$ and $56$ for the evaluation domain,
deterministic curvature and diagnostic maximum.
The vector term uses the exact calculation in the preceding proof
and has coefficient $5c_{\rm vec}$.
The general Bregman remainder is at most $4MD\ell_{\rm ns}/N$.
The local diagnostic error uses
\eqref{eq:threshold-public-moments}. These are the displayed terms.
In the stated evaluation domain regime the evaluation-radius term itself is at most
$28d^{1/4}MD/N$. Use $R_u\le D$, $d^{1/4}\ge1$,
$d^{1/4}\le\sqrt d$ and the variance specialization to obtain
the stated order.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:corrupt-forward-secant}
Draw a uniform-ball $U$ independently of the sampled function indexed by $\xi$.
For $0<\gamma\le\gamma_{\max}/2$, put
\begin{align}
 q_\gamma(y)&=f_{2\gamma}(y)-f_\gamma(y),\nonumber\\
 \widehat q_\gamma^0(y;U,\xi)
 &=F(y+2\gamma U,\xi)-F(y+\gamma U,\xi).
 \label{eq:corrupt-forward-record}
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
 0\le h_\gamma(y)\le q_\gamma(y)\le\mu_dM\gamma.
 \label{eq:corrupt-forward-charge}
\end{equation}
Under the weak-gradient and segment-integrability hypotheses of
Lemma~\ref{lem:oracle-moments}, or a random sample Lipschitz envelope
with second moment at most $M_2^2$, the record satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E \widehat q_\gamma^0(y)=q_\gamma(y),\qquad
 \mathbb E\bigl[\widehat q_\gamma^0(y)^2\bigr]\le\nu_dM_2^2\gamma^2.
 \label{eq:corrupt-forward-moment}
\end{equation}
The corrupted record $\widehat q_\gamma$ differs pointwise from $\widehat q_\gamma^0$
by at most $2\Delta$. For $0<\lambda\le1$,
\begin{equation}
 h_{\lambda\gamma}(y)\le\lambda q_\gamma(y).
 \label{eq:corrupt-forward-shrink}
\end{equation}
The affine lower model for every original comparator $u\in Q$ remains
\begin{equation}
 f(u)\ge f_\gamma(y)+\langle \nabla f_\gamma(y),u-y\rangle-h_\gamma(y).
 \label{eq:corrupt-original-model}
\end{equation}
If the population is $L$-smooth on the evaluation domain, then
$h_\gamma(y)\le L\nu_d\gamma^2$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-affine} proves that $(y,s)\mapsto f_s(y)$ is
jointly convex and differentiable at positive $s$, including evaluation domain
boundary radii. For fixed $y$, write $a(s)=f_s(y)$. Convexity yields
$a(2\gamma)\ge a(\gamma)+\gamma a'(\gamma)$, proving
$h_\gamma(y)\le q_\gamma(y)$. The radial function is even and convex,
so both quantities are nonnegative. Lipschitzness gives
\[
 q_\gamma(y)\le\mathbb E M\gamma\lVert U\rVert=\mu_dM\gamma.
\]
Its sample mean follows by taking the same-sample expectation at both
endpoints.

Under the gradient moment assumption, the fundamental theorem along the sampled
segment gives, almost surely,
\[
 \widehat q_\gamma^0
 =\gamma\int_1^2\langle \nabla F(y+s\gamma U,\xi),U\rangle\,ds.
\]
Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz bound its squared magnitude by
$\gamma^2\lVert U\rVert^2\int_1^2\lVert \nabla F(y+s\gamma U,\xi)\rVert^2ds$.
The segment integrability assumption permits Fubini; integrating in
$\xi,U$ bounds the expectation by
$\gamma^2M_2^2\mathbb E\lVert U\rVert^2=\nu_dM_2^2\gamma^2$.
At an endpoint on the boundary of the evaluation domain, sample continuity
and increasing inner radii give the same conclusion by Fatou. The
uniform second-moment bound supplies uniform integrability for the
mean. Under a random Lipschitz envelope, instead apply
$|\widehat q_\gamma^0|\le m(\xi)\gamma\lVert U\rVert$ directly.

The two corruption values in the record differ by at most $2\Delta$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-affine} gives
$h_{\lambda\gamma}(y)\le\lambda h_\gamma(y)$, proving
\eqref{eq:corrupt-forward-shrink}. Its joint convex affine lower model
at $(y,\gamma)$ applied to $(u,0)$ proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-original-model}. Finally, in the smooth case,
\[
 \partial_\gamma f_\gamma(y)
 =\mathbb E\langle \nabla f(y+\gamma U)-\nabla f(y),U\rangle
 \le L\gamma\mathbb E\lVert U\rVert^2=L\nu_d\gamma,
\]
where $\mathbb E U=0$ cancels the center gradient. Multiplication by $\gamma$
proves the last claim.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:corrupt-controller}
Algorithm~\ref{alg:corrupt-radial} uses exactly $T$ pairs and $2T$
values, $N$ projections, and $3N$ sampling stages with fixed batch sizes or $5N$ with adaptive batch sizes. Its diagnostic and radius satisfy
\begin{align}
 \|\mathsf S_N\|_{L_2}&\le\mu_dM+\omega,
 &\mathbb E\mathsf S_N&\le\mu_dM+\omega,
 \label{eq:corrupt-diagnostic-maximum}\\
 \gamma_t^{-1}
 &\le\min\{g^{-1},
        \max\{\Gamma^{-1},\mathsf S_NN^2/(\underline K_tD^2)\}\},
 \label{eq:corrupt-inverse-path}\\
 \left\|\max_t\gamma_t^{-1}\right\|_{L_2}&\le\zeta.
 \label{eq:corrupt-inverse-moment}
\end{align}
If $J=\sum_t I_t$, then
\begin{equation}
 J\le\log_2\left(1+\frac{H_N-h_{\rm init}}{h_{\rm ref}}\right),
 \qquad
 \sum_{t:I_t=1}\underline K_t\le2(H_N-h_{\rm init}).
 \label{eq:corrupt-reference-cost}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
The trial center and radius are fixed before sampling the diagnostic functions
and directions. The clean
normalized conditional mean is between zero and $\mu_dM$, and its
conditional variance is at most $\nu_dM_2^2/B^{\rm rad}$. Therefore
\[
 \mathsf S_N\le\mu_dM+
 \max_t\left|\widehat q_t^0/\gamma_t^{\rm try}
      -q_{\gamma_t^{\rm try}}(y_t)/\gamma_t^{\rm try}\right|.
\]
The squared maximum is at most the sum of the centered squared
normalized diagnostics. Taking expectations bounds its $L_2$ norm
by $\omega$. Minkowski and Cauchy--Schwarz prove
\eqref{eq:corrupt-diagnostic-maximum}.

The endpoint bound gives
$|\widehat q_t-\widehat q_t^0|\le2\Delta$ pathwise, hence
$[\widehat q_t-2\Delta]_+\le[\widehat q_t^0]_+$.
The exact reciprocal of the protected rule is
\[
 \gamma_t^{-1}=\min\left\{g^{-1},
 \max\left\{(\gamma_t^{\rm try})^{-1},
 \frac{[\widehat q_t-2\Delta]_+}
 {\tau_t\gamma_t^{\rm try}}\right\}\right\}.
\]
At the first iteration of every reference block the trial radius is
$\Gamma$; afterward it is the previous selected radius. Induction,
with the constant threshold in each block, proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-inverse-path}. Since $\underline K_t\ge h_{\rm ref}$,
the pathwise maximum is at most $g^{-1}$ and at most
$\Gamma^{-1}+\mathsf S_NN^2/(h_{\rm ref}D^2)$. Taking its $L_2$ norm
proves \eqref{eq:corrupt-inverse-moment}. These arguments remain valid
when $g=0$, because all selected radii are positive.

Monotonicity of $\mathsf K_t$ and the trigger give
$\underline K_t\le\mathsf K_{t-1}<2\underline K_t$.
Successive replaced reference values increase by a factor at least
two, and the last value is at most
$\mathsf K_N=h_{\rm ref}+H_N-h_{\rm init}$. This gives the count in
\eqref{eq:corrupt-reference-cost}. For consecutive reference values
$c_{j-1},c_j$, $c_j\ge2c_{j-1}$ implies
$c_j\le2(c_j-c_{j-1})$. Summation proves its reference sum.

Finally $B^{\rm rad}\ge T/(16N)$ and $NB^{\rm rad}\le T/8$.
With fixed batch sizes, $\mathsf U_{\rm pub}\ge7T/8\ge7N$; summing its floors gives
$2\sum_t B_t^{\rm pub}\le\mathsf U_{\rm pub}$. Thus the prescribed
residual is nonnegative and makes the two-center update counts exact.
Moreover $B_t^\iota\ge\mathsf U_{\rm pub}t/(2N(N+1))$ for $\iota\in\{y,x\}$.
With adaptive batch sizes $\mathsf U_{\rm emp}\ge5T/8\ge10N$; the adaptive
surplus calculation gives exactly $\mathsf U_{\rm emp}$ update pairs
with $B_t^\iota\ge\mathsf U_{\rm emp}t/(4N(N+1))$. Its pilots cost $4N$
pairs. Adding the $NB^{\rm rad}$ radial pairs gives exactly $T$ in
both modes. Each sampled function contributes two values. Every iteration uses one
radial and two vector stages with fixed batch sizes, or one radial and four
vector sampling stages, plus one projection.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:corrupt-vector-energy}
The actual corrupted vector means satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\sqrt{\mathbb E\mathcal E_N}}D
 \le\frac{c_{\rm vec}\bar\sigma A}{D\sqrt T}
            +\frac{2\beta\sqrt{\mathsf W_{N,2}}}D,
 \qquad
 \frac1A\left|\mathbb E\sum_tZ_t\right|\le2D\beta.
 \label{eq:corrupt-vector-energy}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
At a fixed center and selected radius, decompose a single corrupted
symmetric record into its conditional mean and centered part. The
conditional bias is $b_\gamma$. The dual-norm calculation gives
$\lVert b_\gamma\rVert\le c_d\Delta/\gamma$.
The corruption vector has pointwise norm at most $d\Delta/\gamma$.
Its centered $L_2$ norm is therefore at most the same bound.
Minkowski with the clean centered record proves that the corrupted
centered standard deviation is at most $\sigma_0+d\Delta/\gamma$.
A mean of conditionally independent records has variance equal to the
single-record variance divided by its batch size.

For $\iota\in\{y,x\}$, write $e_t^\iota=b_t^\iota+n_t^\iota$,
where $n_t^\iota=\zeta_t^\iota$ in the notation of
\eqref{eq:conditional} and is centered conditionally on the history preceding
that update mean. The second history
contains the first centered mean, so
$\mathbb E\langle n_t^x,n_t^y\rangle=0$. The expected centered energy is bounded
using the deterministic lower batch floors. Since
\eqref{eq:corrupt-inverse-moment} implies
\[
 \left\|\sigma_0+d\Delta\gamma_t^{-1}\right\|_{L_2}
 \le\bar\sigma,
\]
the floor sums give
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_t t^2\lVert n_t^x-n_t^y\rVert^2\le
 \begin{cases}
 8\bar\sigma^2A^2/\mathsf U_{\rm pub}
          \le(64/7)\bar\sigma^2A^2/T,\\
 16\bar\sigma^2A^2/\mathsf U_{\rm emp}
          \le32\bar\sigma^2A^2/T.
 \end{cases}
\]
Here the randomness of $B_t^\iota$ is harmless because its deterministic
floor holds after the pilot observations choose it.
Both biases have norm at most $c_d\Delta\gamma_t^{-1}$, so
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_t t^2\lVert b_t^x-b_t^y\rVert^2\le4\beta^2\mathsf W_{N,2}.
\]
Minkowski in the weighted vector $L_2$ space proves the energy bound.
This decomposition retains all bias/noise correlations; it cancels
only the cross term between the two centered update means.

The vector $u-v_{t-1}$ precedes $n_t^y$, and $v_t-v_{t-1}$ precedes
$n_t^x$. Their two centered inner products vanish separately.
Each of these displacements has norm at most $D$, and
$\mathbb E\lVert b_t^\iota\rVert\le\beta$. Thus
$|\mathbb E Z_t|\le2tD\beta$. Summation uses $\sum_t t=A$ and proves
the second claim.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:corrupt-local-charge}
Conditionally on the history before the radial stage,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)\mid\mathcal F_t^{\rm rad}]
 \le\tau_t+\eta+4\Delta+w_{\mathrm{reg}}.
 \label{eq:corrupt-local-charge}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Write $q=q_{\gamma_t^{\rm try}}(y_t)$,
$p=[\widehat q_t-2\Delta]_+$, and
$\lambda=1/\max\{1,p/\tau_t\}$. The endpoint bound implies
\[
 q\le\widehat q_t^0+
      |\widehat q_t^0-q|
 \le p+4\Delta+|\widehat q_t^0-q|.
\]
Indeed $\widehat q_t^0\le\widehat q_t+2\Delta\le p+4\Delta$.
If the floor is inactive, Lemma~\ref{lem:corrupt-forward-secant}
gives $h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)\le\lambda q$. Since
$\lambda p\le\tau_t$ and $\lambda\le1$, this is at most
$\tau_t+4\Delta+|\widehat q_t^0-q|$.
If the floor is active, $h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)=h_g(y_t)\le w_{\mathrm{reg}}$.
Either case is bounded by their sum.
The conditional standard deviation of the clean mean is at most
$\sqrt{\nu_d}M_2\gamma_t^{\rm try}/\sqrt{B^{\rm rad}}\le\eta$.
Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz now proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-local-charge}.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:corrupt-growth-drift}
For either applicable case $\mathrm{reg}$,
$\mathbb E(H_N-h_{\rm init})\le\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $\mathbb E J\le\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta$.
For
\[
 \mathcal D_N^+=\sum_{t=2}^NA_{t-1}
 [f_{\gamma_t}(x_{t-1})-f_{\gamma_{t-1}}(x_{t-1})]_+,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mathbb E\mathcal D_N^+}A
 \le\frac{2D^2}{N^2}\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}
                      +(\eta+4\Delta+w_{\mathrm{reg}}+q_{\mathrm{reg}})\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta.
 \label{eq:corrupt-drift}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Fix a realization, and put
$a=c_dM/\Gamma$, $b=c_dM\mathsf S_NN^2/D^2$ and
$\mathfrak H=4a+2\sqrt{2b}$. The radius bound and
$\underline K_t>\mathsf K_{t-1}/2$ imply
\[
 L_t\le a+2b/\mathsf K_{t-1}.
\]
Moreover
$\mathfrak H^2-4a\mathfrak H-8b=8\sqrt2a\sqrt b\ge0$.
Thus $\mathsf K_{t-1}\ge\mathfrak H$ implies
$4L_t\le\mathfrak H$; if $\mathfrak H=0$, the population is
constant and this statement holds directly.

Use the unified shift $\mathfrak B=\mathfrak H+2NM/D$ and
$k_t=[\mathsf K_t-\mathfrak B]_+$. The scalar balance identity
and $H_t\ge\mathsf K_t$ give, when
$\mathsf K_{t-1}\ge\mathfrak H$ and $k_t>0$,
\[
 (H_t-H_{t-1})D^2
 \le[-k_tr_t^2/2+t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t]_+
 \le\frac{t^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2}{2k_t}.
\]
Here the observed secant is bounded by
$A_t\widehat\beta_t\le2L_tr_t^2+
t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t$, exactly as in the original scalar-growth
proof. Since $0\le k_t-k_{t-1}\le H_t-H_{t-1}$, it follows that
\begin{equation}
 D^2(k_t^2-k_{t-1}^2)\le t^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2.
 \label{eq:corrupt-square-recursion}
\end{equation}
The case $k_t=0$ is immediate. If
$\mathsf K_{t-1}<\mathfrak H$, both true gradients have norm at
most $M$, and $r_t\le D$ bounds the coefficient increment by
$t(2M+\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert)/D$. Then $k_{t-1}=0$ and
$k_t\le t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert/D$, proving the same recursion.
Summation gives
\[
 H_N-h_{\rm init}
 \le(\mathfrak H+2NM/D-h_{\rm ref})_+
                        +\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D.
\]
Take expectations, use
$\mathbb E\sqrt{M\mathsf S_N}\le\sqrt{M(\mu_dM+\omega)}$, and apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:corrupt-vector-energy}. This proves the nonsmooth
envelope. Under common population smoothness every target is
$L$-smooth; the original scalar-growth argument gives
$H_N-h_{\rm init}\le4L+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D$, proving the
smooth envelope. Jensen and \eqref{eq:corrupt-reference-cost} yield
$\mathbb E J\le\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta$.

When $I_t=0$, the protected radius cannot increase: its candidate is
at most the previous radius and its floor also is at most that radius.
Thus only reference events have positive target drift. On such an
event the original affine model and $f_{\gamma_{t-1}}\ge f$ give
\[
 [f_{\gamma_t}(x_{t-1})-f_{\gamma_{t-1}}(x_{t-1})]_+
 \le h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)
 +D_{f_{\gamma_t}}(x_{t-1},y_t),
\]
where $D_\phi(x,y)=\phi(x)-\phi(y)-\langle \nabla\phi(y),x-y\rangle$.
The center identity gives
$\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert\le2D/(t+1)$. The Bregman remainder is
at most $2M\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert$, or
$L\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert^2/2$ in the smooth case. After multiplication
by $A_{t-1}$ these bounds are respectively at most $2MDN$ and
$LD^2$, that is $Aq_{\mathrm{reg}}$.

The event and threshold are predictable before the radial
stage. Multiply \eqref{eq:corrupt-local-charge} by $I_tA_{t-1}$
before taking expectations. Since $A_{t-1}\le A$ and the reference
sum is at most $2(H_N-h_{\rm init})$, this gives
\[
 \frac1A\mathbb E\sum_t I_tA_{t-1}h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)
 \le\frac{2D^2}{N^2}\mathbb E(H_N-h_{\rm init})
                      +(\eta+4\Delta+w_{\mathrm{reg}})\mathbb E J.
\]
Adding the Bregman sum and applying the two envelope bounds proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-drift}. No terminal event count is multiplied by
an earlier random diagnostic error.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{thm:corrupt-radial}
Under the stated geometry, clean moment and fixed-corruption assumptions,
Algorithm~\ref{alg:corrupt-radial} satisfies, for every fixed $u\in Q$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{\mathbb E[h_{\rm init}R_u^2]}{2A}
 +k_ND^2\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}+\frac{h_{\rm ref}D^2}{N^2}\nonumber\\
 &+(\eta+4\Delta+w_{\mathrm{reg}})(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)+q_{\mathrm{reg}}\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta+2D\beta,
 \label{eq:corrupt-adaptive-risk}
\end{align}
where $R_u=\lVert u-x^0\rVert$ and the quantities are
\eqref{eq:corrupt-diagnostic-scales}--\eqref{eq:corrupt-curvature-envelopes}.
The nonsmooth branch is always applicable; the smooth branch additionally
assumes population $L$-smoothness on the evaluation domain. The exact counts are
$T$ original pairs, $2T$ values and $N$ projections in $3N$ sequential sampling stages with fixed batch sizes or
$5N$ with adaptive batch sizes.
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
The scalar projection potential is a pathwise statement for arbitrary
observed vector records. Its derivation uses the same selected target
at both centers and the original-objective affine model. Those
conditions hold here. Therefore the changing-target potential is
\begin{align*}
 A[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{h_{\rm init}R_u^2}{2}+2D^2(H_N-h_{\rm init})
 +\sum_t t h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)\\
 &+\mathcal D_N^++\sum_t Z_t.
\end{align*}
This is Theorem~\ref{thm:radial-potential} with its proved arbitrary
vector-error inner products retained; it requires no centering
assumption in the pathwise inequality.
Predictable local-charge averaging and
$\underline K_t\le\mathsf K_N$ give
\[
 \frac1A\sum_t t\mathbb E h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)
 \le\frac{D^2}{N^2}
 [h_{\rm ref}+\mathbb E(H_N-h_{\rm init})]+\eta+4\Delta+w_{\mathrm{reg}}.
\]
Add \eqref{eq:corrupt-drift} and the biased inner-product bound
\eqref{eq:corrupt-vector-energy}, and use
$\mathbb E(H_N-h_{\rm init})\le\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $\mathbb E J\le\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta$.
The three local/drift coefficient contributions are
$2D^2/A+D^2/N^2+2D^2/N^2=k_ND^2$, giving exactly
\eqref{eq:corrupt-adaptive-risk}.
All terms are integrable by Lemmas~\ref{lem:corrupt-controller} and
\ref{lem:corrupt-vector-energy}, and the coefficient envelope.
An initial observed coefficient can be conditioned on its initial
history throughout. The cost claim is
Lemma~\ref{lem:corrupt-controller}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{cor:corrupt-bias-budget}
Fix $\rho>0$. Choose
\begin{equation}
 g=\frac{c_d\Delta D}{\rho}\le\gamma_{\max}/2.
 \label{eq:corrupt-public-floor}
\end{equation}
For $\Delta>0$,
$D\beta\le\rho$ and
$\bar\sigma\le\sigma_0+\kappa_d\rho/D$.
The following explicit bounds hold, with the actual applicable
$\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta$ of \eqref{eq:corrupt-curvature-envelopes}:
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{\mathbb E[h_{\rm init}R_u^2]}{2A}
 +\frac{[(28+2\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta)L+h_{\rm ref}]D^2}{N^2}
 +\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0D}{\sqrt T}\nonumber\\
 &+\left(2+\frac{14}{\sqrt N}
              +\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d}{\sqrt T}\right)\rho
 +(\eta+4\Delta+\nu_dLg^2)(1+\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta)
 \label{eq:corrupt-smooth-explicit}
\end{align}
in the smooth case, and
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{\mathbb E[h_{\rm init}R_u^2]}{2A}
 +\frac{h_{\rm ref}D^2}{N^2}
 +\frac{56c_dMD^2}{\gamma_{\max} N^2}\nonumber\\
 &+\left(\frac{28c_d}{d^{1/4}}+14\sqrt{2c_d}
                       +14+4\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta\right)\frac{MD}{N}
 +\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0D}{\sqrt T}\nonumber\\
 &+\frac{28\sqrt{2c_d}M_2D}{\sqrt T}
 +\left(2+\frac{14}{\sqrt N}
            +\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d}{\sqrt T}\right)\rho\nonumber\\
 &+(\eta+4\Delta+\mu_dMg)(1+\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta)
 \label{eq:corrupt-nonsmooth-explicit}
\end{align}
generally. The diagnostic scale obeys
\begin{equation}
 \eta\le4\sqrt{\nu_d}M_2
 \left(\frac{d^{1/4}D}{\sqrt N\sqrt T}
                         +g\sqrt{N/T}\right).
 \label{eq:corrupt-floor-diagnostic-cost}
\end{equation}
When $\Delta=0$, take $g=0$; then $\beta=0$ and
$\bar\sigma=\sigma_0$, and all displayed $\rho$ terms may be removed.
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
For positive $\Delta$, the inverse-radius bound is at most $g^{-1}$,
so \eqref{eq:corrupt-public-floor} gives
$\beta\le\rho/D$ and
$\bar\sigma\le\sigma_0+(d/c_d)\rho/D$.
Since $A\ge N^2/2$, $A/N^2\le1$, and $\mathsf W_{N,2}\le N^3$,
\begin{align*}
 k_ND^2\frac{c_{\rm vec}\bar\sigma A}{D\sqrt T}
 &\le\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\bar\sigma D}{\sqrt T},\\
 k_ND^2\frac{2\beta\sqrt{\mathsf W_{N,2}}}D
 &\le\frac{14D\beta}{\sqrt N}.
\end{align*}
The direct inner-product term is at most $2\rho$.
The smooth deterministic envelope gives
$4Lk_ND^2\le28LD^2/N^2$ and
$q_{\rm s}\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta\le2L\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta D^2/N^2$.
These inequalities prove \eqref{eq:corrupt-smooth-explicit}.

For the nonsmooth branch,
\[
 \sqrt{M(\mu_dM+\omega)}\le\sqrt{M(M+\omega)}
                                     \le M+\omega/2.
\]
Also $k_N\le7/N^2$, $\Gamma\ge\Gamma_0$, and
\[
 \Gamma^{-1}\le2/\gamma_{\max}+N/(d^{1/4}D),\qquad
 \omega\le4\sqrt{\nu_d}M_2N/\sqrt T\le4M_2N/\sqrt T.
\]
The deterministic coefficients are therefore bounded by
$56c_dMD^2/(\gamma_{\max} N^2)$ and
$(28c_d/d^{1/4}+14\sqrt{2c_d}+14)MD/N$.
The $\omega$ term contributes at most
$28\sqrt{2c_d}M_2D/\sqrt T$, and
$q_{\rm ns}\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta\le4M\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta D/N$.
Combining these with the preceding vector bounds proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-nonsmooth-explicit}.
Finally $B^{\rm rad}\ge T/(16N)$ and
$\Gamma=\max\{g,\Gamma_0\}\le g+d^{1/4}D/N$ prove
\eqref{eq:corrupt-floor-diagnostic-cost}.
For zero corruption, \eqref{eq:corrupt-bias-scales} gives exactly
$\beta=0$ and $\bar\sigma=\sigma_0$, so their additional terms vanish.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- corollary-10: body_md -->
\label{cor:corrupt-accuracy}
Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and choose $\rho=\varepsilon/64$ in
\eqref{eq:corrupt-public-floor}. Suppose $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{reg}}\le\varepsilon/2$,
the appropriate mode budget holds, and
\begin{equation}
 T\ge\left(\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d}{4}\right)^2,
 \qquad
 \Delta\le\frac{\varepsilon\gamma_{\max}}{128c_dD},
 \qquad
 \Delta\le\frac{\varepsilon}{64(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)}.
 \label{eq:corrupt-accuracy-common}
\end{equation}
In the nonsmooth branch additionally assume
\begin{equation}
 \Delta\le
 \frac{\varepsilon^2}
 {1024c_d\mu_dMD(1+\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta)}.
 \label{eq:corrupt-accuracy-nonsmooth}
\end{equation}
In the smooth branch this condition may instead be replaced by
\begin{equation}
 \Delta\le
 \frac{\varepsilon^{3/2}}
 {256c_dD\sqrt{\nu_dL(1+\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta)}}.
 \label{eq:corrupt-accuracy-smooth}
\end{equation}
A constraint with zero $M$ or zero $L$ in its denominator is omitted
because the corresponding floor charge is zero. Then
$\mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le\varepsilon$, with the exact costs of
Theorem~\ref{thm:corrupt-radial}.
<!-- end corollary-10 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
The legal-floor condition in \eqref{eq:corrupt-accuracy-common}
gives $g=64c_d\Delta D/\varepsilon\le\gamma_{\max}/2$.
The scalar corruption term is at most
$4\Delta(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)\le\varepsilon/16$.
For the nonsmooth floor, \eqref{eq:corrupt-accuracy-nonsmooth}
gives
\[
 \mu_dMg(1+\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta)
 =\frac{64c_d\mu_dMD\Delta}{\varepsilon}
                                      (1+\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta)
 \le\varepsilon/16.
\]
The smooth floor condition analogously gives
$\nu_dLg^2(1+\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta)\le\varepsilon/16$.
The direct bias and its curvature contribution obey
$(2+14/\sqrt N)\rho\le16\rho=\varepsilon/4$.
The additional vector variance is at most
$5c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d\rho/\sqrt T\le\varepsilon/16$ by
the first budget condition. Add these quantities to
$\mathcal C_{\mathrm{reg}}\le\varepsilon/2$: their sum is
$15\varepsilon/16<\varepsilon$. Zero corruption only removes terms.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:epsilon-clean-scales}
For $\Delta=0$ and $g=0$, the envelopes and diagnostic scales of
Theorem~\ref{thm:corrupt-radial} satisfy
\begin{align}
 \mathcal H^\Delta_{\rm s}D^2/N^2
   &\le4r_{\rm s}+6r_{\rm st}\le6\mathcal B_{\rm s},\nonumber\\
 \mathcal H^\Delta_{\rm ns}D^2/N^2
   &\le(6+2\sqrt2)r_{\rm ns}+8a_{\rm ns}+6r_{\rm st}
    \le9\mathcal B_{\rm ns},\nonumber\\
 \eta&\le4r_{\rm st},\qquad
 q_{\rm s}\le2r_{\rm s},\qquad
 q_{\rm ns}\le4r_{\rm ns}.
 \label{eq:epsilon-clean-scales}
\end{align}
They hold in both batch modes, including the integer floors and
residual allocation in the stated execution.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Put $A=N(N+1)/2$. Both modes have
$B^{\rm rad}=\lfloor T/(8N)\rfloor\ge T/(16N)$ and
$c_{\rm vec}\le6$. Consequently,
\[
 \omega\le4M_2N/\sqrt T,
 \qquad \eta\le
 4d^{1/4}M_2D/(\sqrt N\sqrt T)\le4r_{\rm st}.
\]
Here $d\ge1$ and $N\ge1$ give
$d^{1/4}/\sqrt N\le\sqrt d$. Also $A/N^2\le1$.
Thus the vector term in $\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}D^2/N^2$ is at most
$6\sigma_0D/\sqrt T$, and the smooth deterministic term is
$4r_{\rm s}$.

For the nonsmooth envelope, $\Gamma=\Gamma_0$ and
\[
 \Gamma^{-1}\le2/\gamma_{\max}+N/(d^{1/4}D),\qquad
 \sqrt{M(\mu_dM+\omega)}\le M+\omega/2.
\]
The first term in the nonsmooth envelope is therefore at most
$8a_{\rm ns}+4r_{\rm ns}$, because $c_d\le\sqrt d$.
Its square-root term is at most
\[
 2\sqrt2r_{\rm ns}
   +4\sqrt2d^{1/4}M_2D/\sqrt T
 \le2\sqrt2r_{\rm ns}+6\sqrt dM_2D/\sqrt T.
\]
The $2MN/D$ term contributes at most $2r_{\rm ns}$.
Together with the vector term these inequalities prove the two
coefficient bounds. Since $6+2\sqrt2<9$, their final simplifications
follow. Finally $A\ge N^2/2$ and $d^{1/4}\ge1$ give the two
$q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ bounds. All floor estimates hold already for $T\ge8N$;
the adaptive-batch branch retains its additional $T\ge16N$ condition.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:epsilon-clean}
Under the clean-oracle assumptions and initialization
\eqref{eq:epsilon-initialization}, define
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_{\rm s}^\varepsilon=\log_2\left(1+
             \frac{6\mathcal B_{\rm s}}{\theta\varepsilon}\right),
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\rm ns}^\varepsilon=\log_2\left(1+
             \frac{9\mathcal B_{\rm ns}}{\theta\varepsilon}\right).
 \label{eq:epsilon-calibrated-logs}
\end{equation}
For every fixed original comparator $u\in Q$, the same execution
satisfies every applicable branch of
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&2\theta\varepsilon
    +(28+2\lambda_{\rm s}^\varepsilon)r_{\rm s}
    +(46+4\lambda_{\rm s}^\varepsilon)r_{\rm st},
 \label{eq:epsilon-clean-smooth}\\
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&2\theta\varepsilon
    +(42+14\sqrt2+4\lambda_{\rm ns}^\varepsilon)r_{\rm ns}
    +56a_{\rm ns}+(46+4\lambda_{\rm ns}^\varepsilon)r_{\rm st}.
 \label{eq:epsilon-clean-nonsmooth}
\end{align}
The counts remain exactly $T$ two-value pairs, $2T$ values and $N$
projections in $3N$ sampling stages with fixed batch sizes or $5N$ with adaptive batch sizes.
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
At zero corruption the floor, bias and scalar corruption terms in
Theorem~\ref{thm:corrupt-radial} vanish. Its startup and reference
terms obey, because $R_u\le D$ and $2A\ge N^2$,
\[
 \frac{h_0R_u^2}{2A}+\frac{h_0D^2}{N^2}
 \le2\theta\varepsilon.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:epsilon-clean-scales} and
\eqref{eq:epsilon-initialization} give
$\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta\le\lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}^\varepsilon$. Also $k_N\le7/N^2$. Multiplying the
coefficient bounds of \eqref{eq:epsilon-clean-scales} by $k_NN^2\le7$,
adding $\eta(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)+q_{\mathrm{reg}}\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta$, and using their remaining
inequalities gives the displayed component bounds directly.
No new oracle observations are required for the initialization or
its interpretation, so all counts are unchanged.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- corollary-11: body_md -->
\label{cor:epsilon-clean-budgets}
Choose the initialization before sampling
\begin{equation}
 h_0=h_{\rm ref}=\frac{4\varepsilon N^2}{77D^2}.
 \label{eq:epsilon-initialization-77}
\end{equation}
If an applicable population budget satisfies
$\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}\le\varepsilon/77$, then
$\mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]<\varepsilon$ for every fixed $u\in Q$.
In particular, sufficient smooth budgets are
\begin{equation}
 N\ge\max\{1,\sqrt{154}\,D\sqrt{L/\varepsilon}\},
 \qquad
 T\ge\left(
  \frac{154(\sigma_0+\sqrt dM_2)D}{\varepsilon}\right)^2,
 \label{eq:epsilon-explicit-smooth-budgets}
\end{equation}
in addition to the appropriate mode condition. Sufficient nonsmooth
budgets are
\begin{align}
 N\ge\max\left\{1,
   \frac{231d^{1/4}MD}{\varepsilon},
   \sqrt{231}\,d^{1/4}D
                     \sqrt{\frac M{\gamma_{\max}\varepsilon}}\right\},
 \qquad
 T\ge\left(
   \frac{231(\sigma_0+\sqrt dM_2)D}{\varepsilon}\right)^2.
 \label{eq:epsilon-explicit-nonsmooth-budgets}
\end{align}
Thus the sufficient orders contain no adaptation logarithm:
\begin{align}
 N_{\rm s}&=O\left(1+D\sqrt{L/\varepsilon}\right),\nonumber\\
 N_{\rm ns}&=O\left(1+\frac{d^{1/4}MD}{\varepsilon}
       +d^{1/4}D\sqrt{\frac M{\gamma_{\max}\varepsilon}}\right),\nonumber\\
 T&=O\left(N+
       \frac{(\sigma_0^2+dM_2^2)D^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right).
 \label{eq:epsilon-clean-complexities}
\end{align}
These are sufficient conditions on budgets fixed before sampling. Accuracy is
interpreted through the population risk bound for the supplied horizon.
<!-- end corollary-11 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
With $\theta=4/77$ and $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}\le\varepsilon/77$,
\eqref{eq:epsilon-calibrated-logs} gives
$\lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}^\varepsilon\le\log_2(13/4)<7/4$ in both branches. The last strict
inequality follows from $13^4=28561<32768=2^7\cdot4^4$.
The nonsmooth coefficients in
\eqref{eq:epsilon-clean-nonsmooth} are therefore bounded above by
$49+14\sqrt2$, $56$, and $53$. Since $\sqrt2<10/7$,
$49+14\sqrt2<69$. The corresponding smooth coefficients are at most
$63/2$ and $53$. The noninitial terms in either branch are strictly
less than $69\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}$ whenever $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}>0$.
Their sum with $2\theta\varepsilon=8\varepsilon/77$ is strictly
less than $\varepsilon$. If $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}=0$, the initial term alone
is at most $8\varepsilon/77<\varepsilon$.

In \eqref{eq:epsilon-explicit-smooth-budgets}, each of $r_{\rm s}$
and $r_{\rm st}$ is at most $\varepsilon/154$. In
\eqref{eq:epsilon-explicit-nonsmooth-budgets}, each of
$r_{\rm ns},a_{\rm ns},r_{\rm st}$ is at most $\varepsilon/231$.
This proves the sufficient conditions. Taking ceilings for integer
budgets, imposing $T\ge8N$ or $T\ge16N$, and using
$(\sigma_0+\sqrt dM_2)^2\le2(\sigma_0^2+dM_2^2)$ gives
\eqref{eq:epsilon-clean-complexities}.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- corollary-12: body_md -->
\label{cor:epsilon-corruption-budgets}
Initialize by \eqref{eq:epsilon-initialization-77}, choose before sampling the
bias allowance $\rho=\varepsilon/64$, and supply $\Delta\ge0$.
Choose
\begin{equation}
 g=\frac{64c_d\Delta D}{\varepsilon},\qquad
 \Gamma=\max\{g,\Gamma_0\}.
 \label{eq:epsilon-corruption-floor}
\end{equation}
Let $\kappa_d=d/c_d$. In addition to the mode condition, assume
\begin{align}
 \mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}&\le\varepsilon/256,
 &T&\ge(5c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d/4)^2,\nonumber\\
 \Delta&\le\frac{\varepsilon\gamma_{\max}}{128c_dD},
 &\Delta&\le\varepsilon/160,\nonumber\\
 T&\ge\frac{25600\nu_dM_2^2g^2N}{\varepsilon^2}.
 \label{eq:epsilon-corruption-common}
\end{align}
In the nonsmooth branch additionally assume
\begin{equation}
 \Delta\le\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2560c_d\mu_dMD};
 \label{eq:epsilon-corruption-nonsmooth}
\end{equation}
in the smooth branch it suffices instead that
\begin{equation}
 \Delta\le\frac{\varepsilon^{3/2}}
                  {64\sqrt{40}\,c_dD\sqrt{\nu_dL}}.
 \label{eq:epsilon-corruption-smooth}
\end{equation}
A condition with $M=0$ or $L=0$ in its denominator is omitted.
Then, for every fixed $u\in Q$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]
   <\left(\frac8{77}+\frac{49}{64}\right)\varepsilon
   <\varepsilon,
 \label{eq:epsilon-corruption-risk}
\end{equation}
with exactly the same pair, value, projection and stage counts.
The reference logarithm satisfies $\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta<3/2$.
<!-- end corollary-12 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
The finite-radius condition gives $g\le\gamma_{\max}/2$. For positive
$\Delta$, Corollary~\ref{cor:corrupt-bias-budget} gives
$D\beta\le\rho$ and
$\bar\sigma\le\sigma_0+\kappa_d\rho/D$.
Since $\Gamma\ge\Gamma_0$, the clean deterministic envelope bounds
of Lemma~\ref{lem:epsilon-clean-scales} remain valid. The additional
vector contributions give
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}D^2/N^2
 \le9\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}+
       \rho\left(\frac{c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d}{\sqrt T}
                       +\frac2{\sqrt N}\right).
 \label{eq:epsilon-corruption-envelope}
\end{equation}
Indeed, $A/N^2\le1$ bounds the added variance contribution,
and $\mathsf W_{N,2}\le N^3$ bounds the bias contribution.
The conditions on $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}},T$, and $N\ge1$ imply
\[
 \frac{\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}D^2}{N^2}
 \le\varepsilon\left(\frac9{256}+
                  \frac1{64}\left(\frac45+2\right)\right)
 =\frac{101\varepsilon}{1280}.
\]
Dividing by $h_0D^2/N^2=4\varepsilon/77$ gives
$\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}/h_0\le7777/5120$.
Since $1+7777/5120=12897/5120<8/3<2^{3/2}$, this proves
$\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta<3/2$. For $\Delta=0$ the same envelope bound holds with
its nonnegative additional term retained, so this conclusion is
also valid.

Write
$\eta_0=4d^{1/4}M_2D/(\sqrt N\sqrt T)\le4r_{\rm st}$ and
$\eta_g=4\sqrt{\nu_d}M_2g\sqrt{N/T}$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:corrupt-floor-diagnostic-cost} gives
$\eta\le\eta_0+\eta_g$.
Using $\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta<3/2$ in the exact component bounds from the clean
proof, the clean noninitial terms are at most
$68\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}$, strictly so when $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}>0$: in the
nonsmooth branch their coefficients are
at most $48+14\sqrt2<68$, $56$, and $52$, and in the smooth
branch they are at most $31$ and $52$. The initial and reference
terms remain at most $8\varepsilon/77$.

The additional vector bias and its curvature contribution are at
most $(2+14/\sqrt N)\rho\le\varepsilon/4$.
The added vector-variance contribution is at most
$5c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d\rho/\sqrt T\le\varepsilon/16$.
The scalar corruption contributes at most
$4\Delta(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)\le10\Delta\le\varepsilon/16$.
Each branch condition gives $w_{\mathrm{reg}}\le\varepsilon/40$, and hence
$w_{\mathrm{reg}}(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)\le\varepsilon/16$.
Finally the last budget condition in
\eqref{eq:epsilon-corruption-common} gives
$\eta_g(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)\le10\sqrt{\nu_d}M_2g\sqrt{N/T}
\le\varepsilon/16$.
Their total is at most $\varepsilon/2$. The clean noninitial
contribution is strictly less than $68\varepsilon/256$, including
when $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}=0$. Adding the clean terms proves
\[
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]
 <\frac{8\varepsilon}{77}
       +\frac{68\varepsilon}{256}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}
 =\left(\frac8{77}+\frac{49}{64}\right)\varepsilon.
\]
All positive-corruption contributions vanish or decrease when
$\Delta=0$. The floor and initialization use no extra observations,
so the original exact cost calculation applies.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
The anchor rule \eqref{eq:joint-main-anchor} is
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-anchor}, with the same anchor batch,
$Q_S$, reserve $D_S=2S$ and initial coefficient $h_{\rm a}$.
Condition on the full anchor history. The execution of
Algorithm~\ref{alg:threshold} with budget $T'$ agrees with
Appendix~\ref{subsec:joint-offset-rule}: its projected updates use step size
$a_t/H_{t-1}$ and its radius selection tracks
$\mathsf K_{t-1}=h_{\rm ref}+H_{t-1}-h_{\rm a}$.
The conditional vector and radial moment assumptions hold at the selected
anchor-selected centers and radii under this conditioning.

Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-moment} proves
$\mathbb E S^2\le S_2^2$ and $\mathbb E S\le S_2$ from the anchor second moment.
Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-clipping} retains the clipped initial
comparator distance and proves both anchor prices, hence their minimum
\eqref{eq:joint-main-saturated-price}. Its full proof bounds the fourth
power of the bounded radius by $r_p^2 S^2$; it assumes no fourth
anchor-record moment. The prices are exactly
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-old-price}--\eqref{eq:run5-distance-best-price}.

Theorem~\ref{thm:run5-distance-joint}, whose proof starts from the
complete offset-controller potential, now applies. Its envelopes and
costs \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-envelopes}--\eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-cost}
are \eqref{eq:adaptive-main-Hns}--\eqref{eq:adaptive-main-U}, with
budget $T'$ and $B^{\rm rad}=\lfloor T'/(8N)\rfloor$.
Its logarithms are the deterministic $\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(2r_0)$, frozen before
averaging any anchor-selected geometry. The smooth conclusion is
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-smooth}. Under
$\gamma_{\max}\ge2d^{1/4}r_p/N$, the evaluation domain is untruncated on the whole
possible radius range and \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-nonsmooth}
applies. Otherwise \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-finite-halo} gives
the stated minimum with \eqref{eq:run5-distance-finite-halo-cost}.
These give the costs \eqref{eq:joint-main-smooth-cost}--\eqref{eq:joint-main-nonsmooth-cost}.
Both applicable bounds hold for the same execution, so their minimum gives
\eqref{eq:joint-main-risk}. Without population smoothness, only the nonsmooth
bound is used, as encoded by $\mathcal J_{\rm s}(S_2)=+\infty$.

The initial batch consumes $B_0$ sampled functions in one stage and $T'\ge T/2$.
Thus the condition for fixed batch sizes gives $T'\ge8N$, and the adaptive-batch condition gives
$T'\ge16N$. Lemma~\ref{lem:threshold-accounting} spends exactly $T'$
later sampled functions in $3N$ or $5N$ stages. Adding the anchor gives $T$ pairs,
$2T$ values and $3N+1$ or $5N+1$ stages. Each optimizer step uses one
intersection projection. All states are initialized once and persist.

It remains to derive the explicit rate \eqref{eq:joint-main-order}.
The budgets give $B^{\rm rad}\ge T/(32N)$, and $\chi_d\le2$ implies
\[
 \omega\le\frac{8M_2N}{\sqrt T},\qquad
 \eta(2S_2)\le\frac{16d^{1/4}M_2S_2}{\sqrt{NT}}.
\]
Here $\omega$ and $\eta$ are defined in Appendix~\ref{sec:run5-distance};
the second inequality follows from
$\Gamma(2S_2)\le2d^{1/4}S_2/N$ for every $\gamma_{\max}>0$.
Also $k_N\le7/N^2$, $k_NA\le5$, and
$c_{\rm vec}\le4\sqrt2$.
Substitution into the exact costs yields
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal U_{\rm s}(2S_2,\ell_{\rm s}^0)
 &\le\frac{4h_{\rm ref}S_2^2}{N^2}
      +\frac{80\sigma_0S_2}{\sqrt T}
      +(1+\ell_{\rm s}^0)\left(
        \frac{112LS_2^2}{N^2}
        +\frac{16d^{1/4}M_2S_2}{\sqrt{NT}}\right),\\
 \mathcal V_{\rm ns}(S_2,\ell_{\rm ns}^0)
 &\le\frac{4h_{\rm ref}S_2^2}{N^2}
      +\frac{80\sigma_0S_2}{\sqrt T}\\
 &\quad+(1+\ell_{\rm ns}^0)\left(
        \frac{112\sqrt d\,MS_2^2}{\gamma_{\max} N^2}
        +\frac{128d^{1/4}MS_2}{N}
        +\frac{176d^{1/4}M_2S_2}{\sqrt T}\right).
\end{align*}
For the first inequality, the curvature and drift coefficients obey
$112+8\ell\le112(1+\ell)$ for $\ell\ge0$.
For the second, they obey
$84+28\sqrt2+8\ell\le128(1+\ell)$, while the radial-noise coefficient
satisfies $112\sqrt2+16(1+\ell)/\sqrt N\le176(1+\ell)$.
The nonsmooth bound using $\mathcal V_{\rm ns}$ holds for every
$\gamma_{\max}>0$ by \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-finite-halo}.
Taking the minimum of the applicable bounds and bounding their logarithmic
factors by $1+\max_{\mathrm{reg}\text{ applicable}}\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^0$
proves \eqref{eq:joint-main-order}. Without population smoothness, only
the nonsmooth bound is used.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
The initial state, predictable reference, forward records and protected
radius in Algorithm~\ref{alg:protected-main} agree exactly with
Algorithm~\ref{alg:corrupt-radial}. The fixed batch-size lower bounds and residual, or
pilot and update budgets, are \eqref{eq:corrupt-public-counts} and
\eqref{eq:corrupt-paid-counts}. Thus their executions coincide when
coupled to the same sampled functions and directions, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:corrupt-radial} applies.

Corollary~\ref{cor:corrupt-bias-budget} expands that finite theorem into
\eqref{eq:corrupt-smooth-explicit} and
\eqref{eq:corrupt-nonsmooth-explicit}. For $u=x^\star$, feasibility
implies $R\le D$, and $2A=N(N+1)\ge N^2$. Hence the startup and
reference terms have sum at most $2h_0D^2/N^2$.
The dimensional inequalities $c_d\le\sqrt d$,
$\sqrt{c_d}\le d^{1/4}$ and
$(d/c_d)^2\le3d$ bound all coefficients by the displayed dimension
orders. The uniform vector assumption gives
$\sigma_0\le\sqrt{Cd}M_2$. Since $d,N\ge1$,
$d^{1/4}/\sqrt N\le\sqrt d$. The diagnostic bound
\eqref{eq:corrupt-floor-diagnostic-cost} is therefore at most a
constant times $\sqrt dM_2D/\sqrt T+M_2g\sqrt{N/T}$.
Also $2+14/\sqrt N\le16$, so the bias-budget terms are bounded by a
constant times $\rho(1+\sqrt{d/T})$.

In the smooth branch the remaining deterministic terms have orders
$LD^2/N^2$ and $Lg^2$, multiplied only by
$1+\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta$. In the nonsmooth branch they have orders
$d^{1/4}MD/N$, $\sqrt dMD^2/(\gamma_{\max} N^2)$ and $Mg$, multiplied
only by $1+\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta$. Both share the previously bounded
sampling, initialization, direct $\Delta$ and bias-budget terms.
Taking the smaller applicable branch proves
\eqref{eq:protected-main-order}. Without smoothness only the nonsmooth
branch and its finite logarithm are used. At $\Delta=0$, the exact
finite bound has $g=\beta=0$, $\bar\sigma=\sigma_0$ and no extra
$\rho$ terms; this is the stated zero-corruption specialization.
Lemma~\ref{lem:corrupt-controller} supplies the exact resource counts.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Take $\Delta=g=0$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:protected-main} and use its
exact zero-corruption specialization. The order is
$\widetilde O(h_0D^2/N^2+\mathcal B_{N,T})$ with only the applicable
reference logarithm suppressed. The assumed initialization gives
$2h_0D^2/N^2\le\mathcal B_{N,T}$, so the explicit sum is at most a
universal constant times $\mathcal B_{N,T}$. This proves the first
claim while retaining its logarithmic reference dependence.
The algorithm requires strict positivity because both its projected
step and radial threshold divide by positive coefficients, but none of
its assumptions imposes a further positive lower bound. Finally,
$h_0\le\varepsilon N^2/(8D^2)$ implies
$2h_0D^2/N^2\le\varepsilon/4$ directly. This choice made before sampling needs no
population smoothness, Lipschitz scale or variance, and does not remove
the logarithms in the finite theorem.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:frontier-conditional}
Under the preceding assumptions, set $\nu=8\sqrt2$ for fixed
batch sizes and $\nu=16\sqrt2$ for adaptive batch sizes. Then
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[\phi(x_N)-\phi(u_S)\mid\text{anchor}]
 \le{}&\frac{h_{\rm a}\min\{R_u^2,S^2\}}{2A}
 +\frac{32L_\gamma S^2}{A}
 +\frac{\nu\sigma_\gamma S}{\sqrt{T'}}.
 \label{eq:frontier-conditional-risk}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
Condition on the complete anchor batch. Its realized $h_{\rm a}$,
$S$, $Q_S$ and $u_S$ are fixed, positive or finite as appropriate.
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:potential} and Lemma~\ref{lem:growth} to
$\phi$ itself, with zero comparator smoothing charge. The initial
potential is $h_{\rm a}\lVert u_S-x^0\rVert^2/2$, where
$\lVert u_S-x^0\rVert^2=\min\{R_u^2,S^2\}$.
Write $e_t^y=g_t^y-\nabla\phi(y_t)$, $e_t^x=g_t^x-\nabla\phi(x_t)$ and
$\mathcal E_N=\sum_tt^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2$.
The scalar coefficient bound is
$H_N-h_{\rm a}\le4L_\gamma+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D_S$.
The fixed batch-size lower bounds satisfy
$B_t^\iota\ge T't/[2N(N+1)]$ for $\iota\in\{y,x\}$ because $T'\ge4N$.
The first mean is known before the second batch is drawn, so conditional
centering gives $\mathbb E[\langle e_t^x,e_t^y\rangle\mid\text{anchor}]=0$.
Thus $\mathbb E[\mathcal E_N\mid\text{anchor}]\le8\sigma_\gamma^2A^2/T'$.
The minimum adaptive batch sizes give instead $32\sigma_\gamma^2A^2/T'$.
Both error inner products in the potential have zero conditional
expectation, since their distance factors are known before the
corresponding batches are drawn. The remaining curvature contribution is
\[
 8L_\gamma D_S^2/A+
 2D_S\sqrt{\mathbb E[\mathcal E_N\mid\text{anchor}]}/A.
\]
Substitution of $D_S=2S$ proves \eqref{eq:frontier-conditional-risk}.
Compactness bounds the distance factors, and the positive reference
and scalar energy bound ensure integrability.

For the accounting with fixed batch sizes,
$2\sum_tB_t^y\le2N+2(T'-2N)\sum_tt/[N(N+1)]=T'$.
The added final labels spend the residual and preserve every floor.
There are two vector stages per optimizer step and one anchor stage.
The adaptive sample count follows Lemma~\ref{lem:paid-accounting} with budget
$T'$. Each record contributes one pair and two values.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- corollary-13: body_md -->
\label{cor:frontier-noise-multiplier}
Under Theorem~\ref{thm:run5-distance-fixed}, with
$\gamma_{\rm a}=\gamma$ and $\sigma_{\rm a}=\sigma_\gamma$, define
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H_p(R)=R+r_0+R^2/(p r_0),\qquad
 P_{\rm up}(p)=\sqrt3+\nu\sqrt2(1+2p).
 \label{eq:frontier-noise-shape}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{h_{\rm ref}\Psi(R_u)}{A}
 +\frac{G_0\Psi(R_u)}{p r_0}
 +\frac{32L_\gamma r_p^2}{A}\nonumber\\
 &+P_{\rm up}(p)\frac{\sigma_\gamma\mathcal H_p(R_u)}{\sqrt T}
 +\beta_\gamma(u).
 \label{eq:frontier-noise-risk}
\end{align}
<!-- end corollary-13 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
Theorem~\ref{thm:run5-distance-fixed} gives
$\mathcal A_*(u)\le\mathcal A_p(u)$ and $S_2\le r_p$.
The admissible budgets give $B_0\ge T/3$ and $T'\ge T/2$.
Since $a_R\le R$ and $\Psi(R)\le5R^2/8$, the anchor noise in
$\mathcal A_p(u)$ is at most
$\sqrt3\sigma_\gamma\mathcal H_p(R)/\sqrt T$.
The remaining noise is at most
$\nu\sqrt2(1+2p)\sigma_\gamma r_0/\sqrt T$, and
$\mathcal H_p(R)\ge r_0$. This proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{thm:frontier-pareto-lower}
Let any algorithm draw at most $n$ independent sampled functions and return
$\widehat x\in Q$, with the same known inputs and internal-randomization
law on both instances. Arbitrary adaptive query endpoints are allowed,
including observation of each entire realized sample function.
Suppose its deterministic-law guarantee is
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_0[m(S-\widehat x)]
 \le\frac{h_{\rm ref}\Psi(R_0)}{A}
 +\frac{m\Psi(R_0)}{p r_0}.
 \label{eq:frontier-affine-contract}
\end{equation}
Suppose also its rare-law guarantee, for some $P\ge0$, is
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E_1[f_1(\widehat x)-f_1(0)]\le{}&
 \frac{h_{\rm ref}\Psi(r_0)}{A}
 +\frac{m(1+1/n)\Psi(r_0)}{p r_0}\nonumber\\
 &+P\frac{\sigma_1\mathcal H_p(r_0)}{\sqrt n}.
 \label{eq:frontier-local-contract}
\end{align}
Writing $q_n=(1-1/n)^n$, necessarily
\begin{equation}
 P\ge\frac{[q_n(1+1/n)(1+p/5)-(2+1/n)/(2p)]_+}
                {2(2+1/p)}.
 \label{eq:frontier-exact-lower}
\end{equation}
In particular $P\ge p/88$ for $p\ge5$.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Since $h_{\rm ref}/A\le m/(p r_0)$ and $\Psi(R_0)\le5R_0^2/8$,
the deterministic-law error bound gives
\[
 \mathbb E_0(S-\widehat x)\le2\Psi(R_0)/(p r_0)
 \le5R_0^2/(4p r_0)=R_0/2.
\]
Thus $\mathbb E_0\widehat x\ge r_0(1+p/5)$.
Generate $n$ independent draws from the second law in advance,
including unused draws if the algorithm stops early. Couple its internal random seed across
the two instances. On the event that all draws select $F_0$,
the entire corresponding functions agree. Induction through the
adaptive transcript gives identical endpoints, batch allocations,
stopping decisions and output. This reasoning also permits repeated
evaluations under one label and full realized-function observation.
The event is independent of internal randomness and has probability
$q_n$. The rare gap is the nonnegative quantity
$m(1+1/n)\widehat x$. Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_1[f_1(\widehat x)-f_1(0)]
 \ge q_n m(1+1/n)r_0(1+p/5).
 \label{eq:frontier-coupled-lower}
\end{equation}

Since $\Psi(r_0)=r_0^2/2$, the deterministic terms in
\eqref{eq:frontier-local-contract} are at most
$m r_0(2+1/n)/(2p)$. Moreover
$\mathcal H_p(r_0)=(2+1/p)r_0$ and $\sigma_1\le2m\sqrt n$,
so its noise term is at most $2P m r_0(2+1/p)$.
Comparison with \eqref{eq:frontier-coupled-lower} proves
\eqref{eq:frontier-exact-lower}.

For completeness, let $g(x)=x\log(1-1/x)$ on $x\ge2$ and
$z=1/(x-1)$. Then
$g'(x)=z-\log(1+z)\ge0$, because
$\log(1+z)=\int_0^z(1+s)^{-1}\,ds\le z$.
Thus $q_n\ge\exp(g(2))=1/4$.
For $n\ge4$ the numerator of \eqref{eq:frontier-exact-lower}
is at least $1/4+p/20-9/(8p)$.
For $p\ge5$ its first and last terms have nonnegative sum,
and the denominator is at most $2(2+1/5)=22/5$.
Hence $P\ge(p/20)/(22/5)=p/88$.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lem:joint-offset-potential}
Condition on the complete anchor batch. For either admissible envelope
$\mathcal H(D)$ in \eqref{eq:joint-curvature-envelopes}, put
$\ell(D)=\log_2(1+\mathcal H(D)/h_{\rm ref})$.
For every conditionally fixed $w\in Q_S$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(w)\mid\text{anchor}]\le{}&
 \frac{h_{\rm a}\lVert w-x^0\rVert^2}{2A}
 +\left(\frac2A+\frac3{N^2}\right)D_S^2\mathcal H(D_S)
 +\frac{h_{\rm ref}D_S^2}{N^2}\nonumber\\
 &+\eta(D_S)[1+\ell(D_S)]
 +\frac{2MD_SN}{A}\ell(D_S).
 \label{eq:joint-conditional-risk}
\end{align}
For the smooth envelope replace the last term by
$LD_S^2\ell(D_S)/A$.
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Under the anchor law the geometry and initial coefficients are fixed.
Let $\mathsf S_N$ be the maximum positive radial mean normalized by its
trial radius. Conditional normalized means lie in $[0,M]$, and their
centered variances are at most $\chi_dM_2^2/B^{\rm rad}$.
Thus $\lVert \mathsf S_N\rVert_{L_2}\le M+\omega_{\rm rad}$ by bounding the squared
error maximum by the sum of squared errors and applying Minkowski.
No independence between iterations is required.

The reference satisfies $\underline K_t\le\mathsf K_{t-1}<2\underline K_t$.
Within a reference block, the reciprocal update is a maximum starting
from $\Gamma_S^{-1}$. Therefore
\begin{align}
 \gamma_t^{-1}&\le
 \max\{\Gamma_S^{-1},\mathsf S_NN^2/(\underline K_tD_S^2)\},\nonumber\\*
 L_t&\le\sqrt d M/\Gamma_S+
       2\sqrt dM\mathsf S_NN^2/(\mathsf K_{t-1}D_S^2).
 \label{eq:joint-reciprocal-control}
\end{align}
Fix a complete realization and define
\[
 \mathfrak K=4\sqrt dM/\Gamma_S+
             2\sqrt2d^{1/4}\sqrt{M\mathsf S_N}\,N/D_S.
\]
Write $a=\sqrt dM/\Gamma_S$ and
$b=\sqrt dM\mathsf S_NN^2/D_S^2$. Then
$\mathfrak K=4a+\sqrt{8b}$ and
$\mathfrak K^2-4a\mathfrak K-8b=4a\sqrt{8b}\ge0$.
Whenever $\mathsf K_{t-1}\ge\mathfrak K$,
\eqref{eq:joint-reciprocal-control} therefore gives
$4L_t\le4a+8b/\mathfrak K\le\mathfrak K$.
If $a=b=0$, every target is affine and the shifted-square argument
below applies directly with threshold zero.
Write $e_t^y=g_t^y-\nabla f_{\gamma_t}(y_t)$, $e_t^x=g_t^x-\nabla f_{\gamma_t}(x_t)$,
$\delta_t=H_t-H_{t-1}$ and
$\mathcal E_N=\sum_tt^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2$.
The scalar balance and secant bound give
\begin{align*}
 \delta_tD_S^2
 &\le[-(H_t-4L_t)r_t^2/2+t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t]_+\\
 &\le[-(\mathsf K_t-\mathfrak K)r_t^2/2
                   +t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t]_+.
\end{align*}
Here $H_t\ge\mathsf K_t$ is essential.
Because $\mathsf K_t-\mathsf K_{t-1}=\delta_t$, completion of
a square gives the positive-part square recurrence after this crossing.
Before it, the gradient-norm envelope and $r_t\le D_S$ give
$\delta_t\le t(2M+\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert)/D_S$.
There is at most one crossing. Its noisy jump and all later energy
combine using $\sqrt{(a+\sqrt q)^2+b}\le a+\sqrt{q+b}$.
Consequently
\[
 H_N-h_{\rm a}=\mathsf K_N-h_{\rm ref}
 \le\mathfrak K+2NM/D_S+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D_S.
\]
If $h_{\rm ref}\ge\mathfrak K$, the square recurrence holds throughout
and gives a stronger bound.
The lower bounds on the vector batch sizes yield
$\sqrt{\mathbb E[\mathcal E_N\mid\text{anchor}]}\le
c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0A/\sqrt{T'}$.
Also $\mathbb E\sqrt{M\mathsf S_N}\le M+\omega_{\rm rad}/2$.
Thus the conditional expected coefficient increase is bounded by
$\mathcal H_{{\rm j},\rm ns}(D_S)$.
Under smoothness, Lemma~\ref{lem:growth} instead gives
$\mathcal H_{{\rm j},\rm s}(D_S)$.

Each nonzero replacement at least doubles the reference. If $J$ is
their number, then
\[
 J\le\log_2(\mathsf K_N/h_{\rm ref}),\qquad
 \sum_{t:I_t=1}\underline K_t\le2(\mathsf K_N-h_{\rm ref})=2(H_N-h_{\rm a}).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-affine} bounds the selected local charge,
conditionally on the history preceding its diagnostic, by
$\underline K_tD_S^2/N^2+\eta(D_S)$ in expectation.
Its weighted average is at most
$D_S^2\mathbb E[\mathsf K_N\mid\text{anchor}]/N^2+\eta(D_S)$.
At a reexpansion event the positive target drift is at most this new
local charge plus the Bregman remainder at $(x_{t-1},y_t)$.
Since $\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert\le2D_S/(t+1)$, the weighted remainder
is at most $2MD_SN$, or $LD_S^2$ under smoothness.
The event is known before its radial stage, so its charge may be averaged
conditionally first. The expected radial drift is at most
$2D_S^2\mathbb E[H_N-h_{\rm a}\mid\text{anchor}]/N^2
+\eta(D_S)\mathbb E[J\mid\text{anchor}]$.

Theorem~\ref{thm:radial-potential} retains this positive target drift
and charges $2D_S^2\mathbb E[H_N-h_{\rm a}\mid\text{anchor}]/A$ for
scalar growth. Combining the preceding terms gives
\eqref{eq:joint-conditional-risk}, after Jensen bounds the event count
by $\ell(D_S)$. Every diagnostic error is averaged at its predictable
event; no product with a future random logarithm is bounded directly.
The moment estimates also ensure integrability.

For adaptive-batch accounting, $T'\ge16N$ gives the original floors and
$\mathsf U\ge5T'/8$. For the accounting with fixed batch sizes, $T'\ge8N$ gives
$B^{\rm rad}\ge T'/(16N)$ and
$\mathsf U_{\rm pub}\ge7T'/8\ge7N\ge4N$.
Its floors yield energy at most $64\sigma_0^2A^2/(7T')$.
Allocating the remaining samples and including the initial batch proves
all stated counts.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:run5-distance-moment}
Under the preceding moment assumption,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E S^2\le S_2^2,\qquad \mathbb E S\le S_2<r_p.
 \label{eq:run5-distance-radius-moments}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Put $a=r_0$, $b=2p r_0$, $k=\kappa$ and
$F(w)=[a+b\sqrt w/(k+\sqrt w)]^2$ for $w\ge0$. It is increasing,
bounded and continuous at zero. At $z=\sqrt w>0$,
\[
 F''(w)=-\frac{bk[3(a+b)z+4ak+ak^2/z]}{2z^2(k+z)^4}<0.
\]
Indeed, writing $s(z)=a+bz/(k+z)$, differentiation gives
$F''=[(s')^2+ss''-ss'/z]/(2z^2)$,
$s'=bk/(k+z)^2$ and $s''=-2bk/(k+z)^3$.
After factoring $bk/(k+z)^4$, the numerator is
$bk-s(k+z)(3+k/z)=-3(a+b)z-4ak-ak^2/z$.
Continuity extends concavity to $[0,\infty)$. Centering gives
$\mathbb E\lVert g_0\rVert^2=G_{\rm a}^2+
\mathbb E\lVert g_0-\nabla f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}(x^0)\rVert^2\le z_{\rm a}^2$.
Jensen and monotonicity therefore yield
$\mathbb E S^2=\mathbb E F(\lVert g_0\rVert^2)\le F(z_{\rm a}^2)=S_2^2$.
Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\mathbb E S\le S_2$. If $z_{\rm a}=0$, then
$g_0=0$ almost surely and $S=r_0$. The strict upper bound follows
from $\kappa>0$ and finite $z_{\rm a}$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:run5-distance-clipping}
If $f\le f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}$ and $f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}$ is convex, then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\left[\frac{h_{\rm a}\lVert u_S-x^0\rVert^2}{2A}
       +f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}(u_S)-f(u)\right]\le\mathcal A_*(u).
 \label{eq:run5-distance-clipping-price}
\end{equation}
The same bound holds with $f(u_S)$ in place of
$f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}(u_S)$.
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Write $\phi=f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}$, $z=\lVert g_0\rVert$ and
$e_0=g_0-\nabla\phi(x^0)$. If $R_u>S$, set $\theta=S/R_u$.
Segment convexity and the tangent inequality at $x^0$ give
\[
 \phi(u_S)-\phi(u)
 \le(1-\theta)[\phi(x^0)-\phi(u)]\le G_{\rm a}(R_u-S).
\]
If $R_u\le S$, the difference is zero. Thus
$\phi(u_S)-f(u)\le G_{\rm a}(R_u-S)_++\beta_{\rm a}(u)$.
Since $|G_{\rm a}-z|\le\lVert e_0\rVert$ and
$S=r_0+(2A/h_{\rm a})z$,
\[
 G_{\rm a}(R_u-S)_+\le
 z[a_{R_u}-(2A/h_{\rm a})z]_++a_{R_u}\lVert e_0\rVert
 \le\frac{h_{\rm a}a_{R_u}^2}{8A}+a_{R_u}\lVert e_0\rVert.
\]
The last inequality maximizes $z(a_{R_u}-cz)$ with $c=2A/h_{\rm a}$;
it holds for every realized positive $h_{\rm a}$.
Bounding the startup distance by $R_u$ gives the charge
$h_{\rm a}\Psi(R_u)/A+a_{R_u}\lVert e_0\rVert+\beta_{\rm a}(u)$.
The inequalities $\mathbb E z\le G_{\rm a}+\sigma_{\rm a}/\sqrt{B_0}$ and
$\mathbb E\lVert e_0\rVert\le\sigma_{\rm a}/\sqrt{B_0}$ prove
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-old-price}.

For the other price retain
$V=\lVert u_S-x^0\rVert^2=\min\{R_u^2,S^2\}$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-moment} gives
$\mathbb E V\le\min\{R_u^2,S_2^2\}$. Pointwise $V^2\le R_u^4$ and
$V^2\le S^4\le r_p^2S^2$, so
$\mathbb E V^2\le\min\{R_u^4,r_p^2S_2^2\}$.
Cauchy--Schwarz consequently gives
\[
 \mathbb E[zV]\le\sqrt{\mathbb E z^2\,\mathbb E V^2}
       \le z_{\rm a}\min\{R_u^2,r_p S_2\}.
\]
Expand $h_{\rm a}$ and use $S\ge r_0$ in the clipping term to obtain
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-saturated-price}. Both prices bound the same
expected charge, so their minimum applies. The original-function
version follows from $f(u_S)\le\phi(u_S)$. The fourth power here is
that of the bounded radius; no fourth anchor moment is assumed.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{thm:run5-distance-fixed}
Use the fixed-radius execution of Section~\ref{subsec:frontier-rule} with
$\gamma_{\rm a}=\gamma$. Assume uniform clean conditional vector
variance $\sigma_\gamma^2$, anchor variance
$\sigma_{\rm a}^2\le\sigma_\gamma^2$, and $L_\gamma$-smoothness of
$f_\gamma$. Put $B_0=\lfloor T/2\rfloor$, $T'=T-B_0$.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le\mathcal A_*(u)+\frac{32L_\gamma S_2^2}A
       +\frac{\nu\sigma_\gamma S_2}{\sqrt{T'}},
 \label{eq:run5-distance-fixed-risk}
\end{equation}
where $\nu=8\sqrt2$ for fixed batch sizes and $16\sqrt2$ for adaptive batches.
With fixed batch sizes, $T\ge8N$ uses exactly $T$ pairs, $2T$ values, $2N+1$ sampling
stages and $N$ ball-intersection projections. With adaptive batch sizes, $T\ge16N$ gives
$4N+1$ stages and the same other counts.
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Condition on the complete anchor. Lemma~\ref{lem:frontier-conditional}
gives
\[
 \mathbb E[f_\gamma(x_N)-f_\gamma(u_S)\mid\text{anchor}]
 \le\frac{h_{\rm a}\min\{R_u^2,S^2\}}{2A}
       +\frac{32L_\gamma S^2}A
       +\frac{\nu\sigma_\gamma S}{\sqrt{T'}}.
\]
Add $f_\gamma(u_S)-f(u)$ and use $f(x_N)\le f_\gamma(x_N)$.
Taking expectation, Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-clipping} bounds the
sum of the startup and comparator charges by $\mathcal A_*(u)$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-moment} gives $\mathbb E S^2\le S_2^2$ and
$\mathbb E S\le S_2$, proving \eqref{eq:run5-distance-fixed-risk}.
The allocation is unchanged: the anchor and two stages with fixed batch sizes or four with adaptive
batch sizes per optimization iteration use all $T$ sampled functions, with two values for each
sampled function and one intersection projection per iteration. The required budgets
ensure $T'\ge4N$ or $8N$, respectively, as used in the conditional lemma.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\label{thm:run5-distance-joint}
For a smooth population,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le\mathcal A_*(u)
       +\mathcal U_{\rm s}(2S_2,\ell_{\rm s}^0).
 \label{eq:run5-distance-joint-smooth}
\end{equation}
If $\gamma_{\max}\ge2d^{1/4}r_p/N$, the nonsmooth branch satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le\mathcal A_*(u)
       +\mathcal U_{\rm ns}(2S_2,\ell_{\rm ns}^0).
 \label{eq:run5-distance-joint-nonsmooth}
\end{equation}
At every finite permitted evaluation radius it also satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le\mathcal A_*(u)+
 \min\{\mathcal U_{\rm ns}(2r_p,\ell_{\rm ns}^0),
             \mathcal V_{\rm ns}(S_2,\ell_{\rm ns}^0)\}.
 \label{eq:run5-distance-joint-finite-halo}
\end{equation}
With fixed batch sizes, $T\ge16N$ uses exactly $T$ pairs, $2T$ values, $3N+1$ sampling
stages and $N$ ball-intersection projections. With adaptive batch sizes, $T\ge32N$ gives
$5N+1$ stages and the same other counts.
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Conditional on the full anchor, Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-offset-potential}
gives the startup charge plus $\mathcal U_{\mathrm{reg}}(D_S,\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(D_S))$, where
$\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(D)=\log_2(1+\mathcal H_{\mathrm{reg}}(D)/h_{\rm ref})$.
Add clipping and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-clipping}, in its
original-function version. Since $D_S\ge2r_0$ and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{reg}}$ is
decreasing, $\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(D_S)\le\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^0$. Its coefficients are nonnegative;
replace the logarithm by this deterministic bound before averaging.

For the smooth envelope, $D^2\mathcal H_{\rm s}(D)=4LD^2+vD$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-moment} gives
$\mathbb E D_S^2\le4S_2^2$ and $\mathbb E D_S\le2S_2$.
The reference and smooth target-drift terms are multiples of $D^2$.
The function $\eta(D)$ is increasing and concave, as a positive
multiple of the minimum of a constant and a linear map. Jensen gives
$\mathbb E\eta(D_S)\le\eta(\mathbb E D_S)\le\eta(2S_2)$.
These substitutions prove \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-smooth}.

Under the untruncated-evaluation domain condition, every anchor outcome has
$\Gamma(D_S)=d^{1/4}D_S/N$. Thus
$D^2\mathcal H_{\rm ns}(D)=(4d^{1/4}MN+C_{\rm ns})D$,
and this term, $q_{\rm ns}$ and $\eta$ are linear on the whole observed
range. Their first moments and the reference term's second moment
give \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-nonsmooth}.

For an arbitrary finite evaluation domain, pointwise
\[
 \frac{D^2}{\Gamma(D)}
 =\max\left\{\frac{D^2}{\gamma_{\max}},\frac{ND}{d^{1/4}}\right\}
 \le\frac{D^2}{\gamma_{\max}}+\frac{ND}{d^{1/4}}.
\]
Use both radius moments here and in the other linear and quadratic
terms, and use concavity for $\eta$. The result is exactly
$\mathcal V_{\rm ns}(S_2,\ell_{\rm ns}^0)$.
Independently, $D_S\le2r_p$ and monotonicity of each cost factor at
fixed logarithm give $\mathcal U_{\rm ns}(2r_p,\ell_{\rm ns}^0)$.
Each cost bound can be combined with either anchor-price bound,
because they bound separate expected charges. Taking both minima
proves \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-finite-halo}.
All algorithmic stages and allocation rules remain those of the
joint controller, including the anchor and each three-stage iteration with fixed batch sizes
or five-stage iteration with adaptive batch sizes.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- corollary-14: body_md -->
\label{cor:run5-distance-stationary}
Under the smooth assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:run5-distance-joint},
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le\mathcal A_*^{\rm stat}(R_u)
       +\mathcal U_{\rm s}(2S_{R_u},\ell_{\rm s}^0).
 \label{eq:run5-distance-stationary-risk}
\end{equation}
If $\nabla f$ is affine on the evaluation domain, replace $G_{R_u}$ by $LR_u$ and $z_{R_u}$
by $\sqrt{L^2R_u^2+\sigma_{\rm a}^2/B_0}$ in these formulas. The smoothing
excess bound remains $L\nu_d\gamma_{\rm a}^2/2$.
<!-- end corollary-14 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Let $U$ be uniform on the unit ball. Smoothness permits differentiation
under the bounded ball integral. Jensen, original stationarity and
gradient Lipschitz continuity give
\begin{align*}
 G_{\rm a}^2
 &=\lVert \mathbb E_U\nabla f(x^0+\gamma_{\rm a}U)\rVert^2\\
 &\le\mathbb E_U\lVert \nabla f(x^0+\gamma_{\rm a}U)-\nabla f(u)\rVert^2\\
 &\le L^2\mathbb E_U\lVert x^0-u+\gamma_{\rm a}U\rVert^2
 =L^2(R_u^2+\nu_d\gamma_{\rm a}^2).
\end{align*}
Here $\mathbb E U=0$ and $\mathbb E\lVert U\rVert^2=\nu_d$.
Ball averaging of the smooth upper model at $u$ yields
$\beta_{\rm a}(u)\le L\nu_d\gamma_{\rm a}^2/2$.
Both prices are increasing in the nonnegative quantities
$G_{\rm a},z_{\rm a},S_2,\beta_{\rm a}(u)$, and the smooth cost at a
fixed nonnegative logarithm is increasing in $D$. Substitution into
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-smooth} proves the result.
If the gradient is affine, symmetry gives
$\nabla f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}(x^0)=\nabla f(x^0)$, and original
stationarity yields $G_{\rm a}\le LR_u$. No distance to a smoothed
minimizer is assumed.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- corollary-15: body_md -->
\label{cor:run5-distance-reference-absorption}
Under Theorem~\ref{thm:run5-distance-joint}, for each applicable regularity case $\mathrm{reg}$, the saturated-price branch gives
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{z_{\rm a}\min\{R_u^2,r_p S_2\}}{2pr_0}
 +G_{\rm a}a_{R_u}+\beta_{\rm a}(u)
 +\mathcal J_{\mathrm{reg}}^0(S_2)
 +\frac{5h_{\rm ref}r_p^2}{N^2}.
 \label{eq:run5-distance-absorbed-risk}
\end{align}
For any target $\varepsilon>0$ chosen before sampling, the choice
$0<h_{\rm ref}\le\varepsilon N^2/(20r_p^2)$ makes the final term
at most $\varepsilon/4$. It needs no supplied original distance,
domain diameter, smoothness or variance.
<!-- end corollary-15 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
Theorem~\ref{thm:run5-distance-joint} permits the saturated price instead
of its minimum with $\mathcal A_p(u)$. Its explicit startup reference
term satisfies
\[
 \frac{h_{\rm ref}\min\{R_u^2,S_2^2\}}{2A}
 \le\frac{h_{\rm ref}r_p^2}{N^2},
\]
because $S_2\le r_p$ and $2A=N(N+1)\ge N^2$.
In the smooth or untruncated nonsmooth cost, the other explicit
reference term is $4h_{\rm ref}S_2^2/N^2$, at most
$4h_{\rm ref}r_p^2/N^2$.
For a finite nonsmooth evaluation domain, the two candidate geometry bounds have
reference terms $4h_{\rm ref}r_p^2/N^2$ and
$4h_{\rm ref}S_2^2/N^2$. Both are bounded by the former.
For any real $b_1,b_2$ and $q_1,q_2\le q$,
$\min\{b_1+q_1,b_2+q_2\}\le\min\{b_1,b_2\}+q$.
Apply this identity to the finite-radius minimum. In every regime the
remaining geometry cost is bounded by
$\mathcal J_{\mathrm{reg}}^0(S_2)+4h_{\rm ref}r_p^2/N^2$.
Adding the startup bound proves
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-absorbed-risk}.
Finally $r_p=r_0(1+2p)$ depends only on inputs chosen before sampling, so the specified
positive reference choice makes its displayed polynomial charge at
most $\varepsilon/4$ without knowledge of the problem scales.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:run5-distance-curved}
The fixed-radius anchor optimizer satisfies
\begin{equation}
 v_1=x_1=q,\qquad v_t=0,\quad x_t=q/A_t\quad(2\le t\le N),
 \label{eq:run5-distance-quadratic-trajectory}
\end{equation}
and hence
\begin{equation}
 f_L(x_N)-f_L(u)=\frac L2(q/A-G/L)^2\ge\frac{Lq^2}{8A^2}.
 \label{eq:run5-distance-quadratic-risk}
\end{equation}
The joint radial controller has the same optimizer trajectory at every
selected legal radius. Vector and anchor variances are zero.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
In one dimension, for either $e\in\{-1,1\}$ and every radius,
\[
 \frac{f_L(z+\gamma e)-f_L(z-\gamma e)}{2\gamma}e=L(z-R).
\]
All vector means are exact. The anchor is $-G$ and selects
$h_{\rm a}=h$ and the displayed $S$. The first projected vector is
$q\in Q$, with $x_1=q$. For $D_S=2S$ its post coefficient is
\[
 H_1=h+\kappa_q(L-h/2),\qquad
 \kappa_q=\frac{q^2}{D_S^2+q^2/2}<\frac1{16A^2}\le\frac1{16}.
\]
The second center is $y_2=q$. Its tentative vector
$q-2(Lq-G)/H_1$ is nonpositive when
$(2-\kappa_q)L\ge(3-\kappa_q/2)h$.
The assumption $L\ge2Ah\ge2h$ suffices because
$2(2-\kappa_q)-(3-\kappa_q/2)=1-3\kappa_q/2>0$.
Thus $v_2=0$, $x_2=q/A_2$. If the claim holds at $t-1\ge2$, then
$y_t=q/A_t\ge q/A\ge2G/L=2R$, so its gradient is positive.
From $v_{t-1}=0$ projection sends the tentative negative point to zero,
and averaging gives $x_t=q/A_t$. This proves the trajectory by
induction; for $N=1$ the first step alone suffices. Since
$R\le q/(2A)$, the risk bound follows.

Every selected-radius vector gradient is identical in the joint
controller. Its projected vectors, averaged iterates, scalar inner
products and post coefficients are consequently identical; radial
stages change only radii and references. A deterministic sample
Lipschitz envelope on an open neighborhood of the finite evaluation domain is
$M_{2,L}=L(S+\gamma_{\max}+r_0)+G$. This supplies all radial moments at
legal radii. Independent draws from this point-mass distribution satisfy the two-value
same-sample oracle model.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- corollary-16: body_md -->
\label{cor:run5-distance-curved-transfer}
For this fixed-radius family there are no finite $C,E_0\ge0$ depending
only on the fixed known inputs and $G$ such that, uniformly in $L$,
\begin{equation}
 f_L(x_N)-f_L(u)\le\frac{h_{\rm ref}\Psi(R)}A+
 \frac{G\Psi(R)}{p r_0}+\frac{CLR^2}A+\beta_\gamma(u)+E_0.
 \label{eq:run5-distance-invalid-transfer}
\end{equation}
This remains false if $C$ is multiplied by any fixed polynomial in
$\log(1+L/h_{\rm ref})$.
<!-- end corollary-16 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Since $R\le r_0$, $\Psi(R)=R^2/2$, and the first two proposed charges
sum to $hR^2/(2A)$. Quadratic ball smoothing in dimension one gives
$\beta_\gamma(u)=L\gamma^2/6\le Lq^2/(24A^2)$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:run5-distance-curved} therefore gives
\[
 f_L(x_N)-f_L(u)-\beta_\gamma(u)\ge\frac{Lq^2}{12A^2}.
\]
The remaining proposed right side is
$hG^2/(2AL^2)+CG^2/(AL)+E_0$, which remains bounded as $L\to\infty$.
The left side diverges. A fixed logarithmic polynomial times $1/L$
still tends to zero, proving the last assertion.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:prestep-relative-moments}
Suppose the population expectations exist at the queried points.
Assume the weak-gradient, segment-integrability and uniform
sample-gradient second-moment bound with envelope $M_2^2$ on the
evaluation domain, or a random sample Lipschitz envelope with second
moment at most $M_2^2$. Then, at every fixed $x,y\in Q$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E P_\gamma(x,y)=\phi(x)-\phi(y),\qquad
 \mathbb E P_\gamma(x,y)^2\le M_2^2\lVert x-y\rVert^2.
 \label{eq:prestep-value-moments}
\end{equation}
\nopagebreak[4]
An average of $B^q$ conditionally independent records consequently has
centered conditional variance at most
$M_2^2\lVert x-y\rVert^2/B^q$.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Taking expectations of the same sampled function at both endpoints, followed by the
ball average, gives the mean. Under the gradient assumptions, the
fundamental theorem along the shifted segment gives
\[
 P_\gamma(x,y)=\int_0^1
 \langle \nabla F(y+\gamma U+s(x-y),\xi),x-y\rangle\,ds
\]
almost surely. The shifted segment remains in the convex evaluation
domain. Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz give a bound by
$\lVert x-y\rVert^2\int_0^1
\lVert \nabla F(y+\gamma U+s(x-y),\xi)\rVert^2ds$
for the squared record. The segment-integrability assumption permits
Fubini and yields the claimed second moment. At a largest legal
boundary radius, sample continuity and increasing inner radii yield
the same bound by Fatou; uniform second moments give uniform
integrability for the mean. Under the alternative Lipschitz assumption,
the pointwise inequality
$|P_\gamma(x,y)|\le m(\xi)\lVert x-y\rVert$ proves the bound directly.
Conditional independence and centering of the $B^q$ records divide their
variance by $B^q$.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
\label{thm:prestep-potential}
Let $\phi$ be convex and differentiable on $Q$. For arbitrary vector
means and relative-value records define
\begin{equation}
 e_j=g_j-\nabla\phi(y_j),\qquad
 \zeta_j^q=\widehat q_j-[\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)],\qquad
 Z_j(u)=a_j\langle e_j,u-v^-\rangle-A_j^+\zeta_j^q .
 \label{eq:prestep-errors}
\end{equation}
For every fixed $u\in Q$, if $n$ trials have been accepted, then
\begin{equation}
 A_n[\phi(x_n)-\phi(u)]
       +\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-v_n\rVert^2
 \le\frac{h_0}{2}R_u^2
       +\sum_{j\in\mathcal A}\chi_j
       +\sum_{j\in\mathcal A}Z_j(u),
 \qquad R_u=\lVert u-x^0\rVert.
 \label{eq:prestep-pathwise-potential}
\end{equation}
If $\phi=f_\gamma\ge f$, the same fixed original comparator satisfies
\begin{align}
 A_n[f(x_n)-f(u)]+\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-v_n\rVert^2
 \le{}&\frac{h_0}{2}R_u^2+
       \sum_{j\in\mathcal A}[\chi_j+Z_j(u)]
       +A_n\beta_\gamma(u),\nonumber\\
 &\beta_\gamma(u)=f_\gamma(u)-f(u).
 \label{eq:prestep-original-potential}
\end{align}
The comparator need not minimize the smoothed population.
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Projection optimality gives, at any trial,
\[
 a_j\langle g_j,v_j^+-u\rangle
 \le\frac{h_0}{2}\left(
 \lVert u-v^-\rVert^2-\lVert u-v_j^+\rVert^2-\lVert w_j\rVert^2\right).
\]
The center identity and convexity at $y_j$ give
\[
 A^-\phi(x^-)+a_j\phi(u)
 \ge A_j^+\phi(y_j)
             +a_j\langle \nabla\phi(y_j),u-v^-\rangle.
\]
Also $A_j^+(x_j^+-y_j)=a_jw_j$. Combining these identities, writing
$\nabla\phi(y_j)=g_j-e_j$, and adding the distance potential yields
\begin{align*}
 &A_j^+[\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(u)]
                    +\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-v_j^+\rVert^2\\
 &\quad\le A^-[\phi(x^-)-\phi(u)]
                    +\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-v^-\rVert^2\\
 &\qquad\quad+
 A_j^+\bigl[\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)
                       -\langle g_j,x_j^+-y_j\rangle\bigr]
       -\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert w_j\rVert^2
       +a_j\langle e_j,u-v^-\rangle.
\end{align*}
On an accepted trial, substitute the observed model inequality
\eqref{eq:prestep-acceptance} and
$\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)=\widehat q_j-\zeta_j^q$.
The last three terms are bounded by $\chi_j+Z_j(u)$.
Rejected trials do not change the accepted state. Summing only the
accepted transitions, using $A_0=0$, proves
\eqref{eq:prestep-pathwise-potential}. Finally,
$f(x_n)-f(u)\le\phi(x_n)-\phi(u)+\beta_\gamma(u)$ proves
\eqref{eq:prestep-original-potential}. At $n=0$ the potential is its
initial value and both claims hold as equalities or inequalities
directly.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:prestep-rejection-charge}
Suppose $Q$ is compact, $\phi$ is continuously differentiable on $Q$,
$K_{\rm tr}<\infty$, and all vector means and relative-value means
satisfy uniform finite conditional second-moment envelopes under
the histories preceding their respective batches. Assume their conditional means are respectively
$\nabla\phi(y_j)$ and $\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)$.
The curvature candidate is nondecreasing and at least
$\mathcal L_0>0$. Suppose additionally that the nonnegative
allowances have integrable total. Then all potential and error terms
below are integrable, and
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E\left[A_n[\phi(x_n)-\phi(u)]
                  +\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-v_n\rVert^2\right]
 \le{}&\frac{h_0}{2}R_u^2
        +\mathbb E\sum_{j\in\mathcal A}\chi_j
        -\mathbb E\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}Z_j(u).
 \label{eq:prestep-rejection-expectation}
\end{align}
This is a weighted guarantee with a random terminal $A_n$.
The rejected-error term records the dependence introduced by model
selection.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
We first justify integrability under a uniform second-moment
envelope, as in the stated oracle assumptions. Let
$c=h_0/\mathcal L_0$. From \eqref{eq:prestep-weight},
$a_j\le c+\sqrt{cA^-}$. By induction on the number $t$ of accepted
states, $A_t\le c(t+1)^2$: the bound at $t=0$ is immediate, and
$A_{t+1}\le c[(t+1)^2+(t+1)+1]\le c(t+2)^2$.
Thus every executed candidate has
$a_j\le c(K_{\rm tr}+2)$ and
$A_j^+\le c(K_{\rm tr}+2)^2$.
The accepted and tentative points belong to the compact set $Q$;
$\phi$ and all distances are bounded there. Uniform conditional
second moments, these weight bounds and the finite trial cap make
every $Z_j(u)$ integrable.

The execution indicator of each trial, its weight, first center and
$u-v^-$ are known before its vector samples are drawn. Therefore the
expectation of its first error inner product is zero. Its tentative
second center and $A_j^+$ are known before the function-difference samples are drawn, so the expectation of the second error term is zero separately.
Summing over the at most $K_{\rm tr}$ executed trials gives
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_{j\in\mathcal A\cup\mathcal R}Z_j(u)=0.
\]
No accepted or rejected indicator was included in these separate
centering steps. Since their sums partition every executed trial,
$\mathbb E\sum_{\mathcal A}Z_j=-\mathbb E\sum_{\mathcal R}Z_j$.
Taking expectations of \eqref{eq:prestep-pathwise-potential} proves
\eqref{eq:prestep-rejection-expectation}.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\label{thm:prestep-exact-distance}
Suppose $\phi$ is convex and $L$-smooth on $Q$, each $g_j$ equals
$\nabla\phi(y_j)$, each $\widehat q_j$ equals
$\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)$, and $\chi_j=0$.
Let the first curvature candidate be $\mathcal L_0$ and carry it
across successes, doubling it only on rejections. Define
\[
 J_\star=\left\lceil
       \log_2\max\{1,L/\mathcal L_0\}\right\rceil,\qquad
 \overline{\mathcal L}=\max\{\mathcal L_0,2L\}.
\]
A trial cap $K_{\rm tr}\ge N+J_\star$ guarantees $N$ acceptances.
There are at most $J_\star$ rejected trials, every curvature
candidate is at most $\overline{\mathcal L}$, and
\begin{equation}
 A_N\ge\frac{h_0N^2}{4\overline{\mathcal L}},\qquad
 \phi(x_N)-\phi(u)
 \le\frac{h_0R_u^2}{2A_N}
 \le\frac{2\overline{\mathcal L}R_u^2}{N^2}
 \label{eq:prestep-exact-rate}
\end{equation}
for every fixed $u\in Q$. The coefficient and the accepted trajectory
persist throughout. Each rejected trial has the full pair, stage and
projection costs stated in the execution.
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Smoothness and the center identity give
\begin{align*}
 A_j^+\bigl[\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)
             -\langle \nabla\phi(y_j),x_j^+-y_j\rangle\bigr]
 &\le \frac{LA_j^+}{2}\lVert x_j^+-y_j\rVert^2\\*
